findings.proposalGuidance: PHB pp. 30–32: open-hand killing is a separate roll after a successful hit and stun; the source excludes undead and creatures hit only by magical weapons and sets victim hit-dice/hit-point limits. Monks gain no Strength bonus to hit probability or damage.
findings.evidence: Printed p.30 (PDF p.31) gives the open-hand stun/kill sequence: the monk must hit, stun the target, and then succeed on the separate kill percentile roll. Printed p.32 (PDF p.33) describes a distinct once-per-week quivering-palm ability: the monk must touch the intended victim within three melee rounds; it has no effect on undead or creatures hit only by magical weapons and has hit-dice/hit-point limits.
findings.problem: The current sentence attaches p.32 quivering-palm exclusions and limits to the p.30 open-hand kill roll, merging two distinct abilities. It also omits the p.32 once-per-week and touch-within-three-rounds conditions.
findings.requestedCorrection: Split this into separate source-qualified statements for the p.30 open-hand stun/kill procedure and the p.32 quivering palm. Keep the target exclusions and HD/HP limits with quivering palm, and include its weekly use and touch deadline if describing that ability.

findings.proposalGuidance: PHB p. 21: druids cannot turn or control undead, demons, or devils. A 7th-level druid can change into reptile, bird, or mammal forms up to three times daily, once per creature type per day; each change heals 10–60% of previously sustained hit-point damage.
findings.evidence: Printed p.21 (PDF p.22) says the druid becomes the assumed creature in all respects save the mind; the permitted form size ranges from very small animals up to a black bear about twice the druid’s weight. It also sets the daily/type and prior-damage restoration conditions captured in the summary.
findings.problem: The new guidance leaves the size range and retained-mind condition unstated, so its broad wording can imply unrestricted animal size and loss of the druid’s mind.
findings.requestedCorrection: Add the source’s size and retained-mind constraints, or narrow the statement so it is explicitly only a reminder and does not imply those omitted permissions.

findings.evidence: Printed p.22 (PDF p.23) footnotes the four-weapon item cap: a magic bow and magic arrows together count as one weapon.
findings.problem: The guidance lists a maximum of four weapons but omits this counting exception, which affects how the stated cap is applied.
findings.requestedCorrection: Add the bow-and-arrows counting rule, or identify the item-count summary as omitting that exception.
